corrections.issue: Mixes two speakers and their opposite reactions. Mark says he was surprised by the falls in currency and CTA non-trend interest. Niels says he is not surprised by CTA non-trend (short-term managers have done poorly; interest should go to trend, positive five years in a row) and only a little surprised by currency, because trend followers have made more currency P&L over the past 6-12 months (like cocoa suddenly coming alive), while currency managers must first make money to attract interest.
corrections.fix: Mark: interest in currency and non-trend CTA strategies fell, which surprised him given central bank divergence and dispersion. Niels: not surprised by non-trend CTA (short-term managers have done poorly and trend has had five positive years in a row); somewhat surprised by currency since trend followers have made more currency P&L in the last 6-12 months.

completeness_estimate: 0.85 - the first reader captured the survey findings, de-globalisation view, macro-vs-price debate and the VUCA mapping well; missed several smaller points (storytelling reason, survey vs flows, magazine-cover contrarian signal, sector composition caveat, yield-curve ambiguity, uncertainty and risk-taking) and blended two speakers in one claim.
